questions.q: THE SPARKLINE. The ACs 'trend sparkline consistent with existing card styling' and 'exactly one funnel query per resolved window' cannot both be met by any mechanism that exists in this repo. Every DashboardWidget card's chartSeries() reads getMonthlyData(), which is literally up to 13 separate cached queries -- the multiplication this ticket forbids. The two non-DashboardWidget siblings (StagingLiveHitLeader, RecoveryLeader) dodge it by reading cache buckets a DIFFERENT card independently maintains for its own cheap purposes, and no such sibling writer exists for a case-claim/repo funnel. Which way do you want it?
questions.answer: RESOLVED by prod-scale measurement (see perf-measurement.md). Use ONE query grouped by toStartOfMonth(...) over a 3-month span -- the okf house pattern (BatchMonthlySparklineData, okf/concepts/client-analytics.md:83), whose own default span is 3 months. Measured interleaved n=8 on the worst-case org: 1-month median 5.04s / p90 5.54s vs 3-month median 5.40s / p90 6.22s -- the span costs +7% at the median. Nothing prunes (billing_events and hotlist_status_log are both ORDER BY id), so the scan is the same size regardless of window and only the small surviving row count grows. This satisfies BOTH ACs: literally one query per resolved window, and a real trend series consistent with existing card styling. SUPERSEDED AND STRENGTHENED: my +7% was wall-clock contention, not cost. Measured server-side, read_rows is IDENTICAL across 1-, 3- and 13-month windows -- a wider window is genuinely free, because nothing prunes.
options: (a) No real sparkline -- flat/empty series. Zero extra queries, satisfies the one-query AC literally, but not the styling AC's spirit.

(b) Two-point series: this window vs the previous window, as one CTE with conditional aggregation. Still honestly one query. Gives a direction arrow rather than a trend curve. DRIVER'S PICK -- it is the only option that satisfies both ACs as written without new unmeasured cost.

(c) One wide GROUP BY month query producing all 13 buckets in a single round trip, long TTL. Architecturally 'one query' but scans far more than one window, and its cost is completely unmeasured on a 389M-row join. Never authorised by the ticket.

questions.q: Were the ClickHouse numbers in comment 39117 (deduped 11,975 / DB repos 9,130) computed WITHOUT `FINAL` and without `_peerdb_is_deleted = 0` on the hotlist leg? The driver measured production read-only: zod.public_hotlist raw = 154,553,066 vs FINAL+not-deleted = 136,362,585, a 13.3% overcount (~6.18M soft-deleted, ~12.0M unmerged duplicates). The ticket's cited 156,096,149 sits on the RAW lineage and is 12.6% above the FINAL count. If the funnel shared that methodology, its +14-over-target DB repos figure may be an un-deduplicated join reading high -- NOT the benign live-hotlist drift the ticket attributes it to. Both explanations fit +14 and they mean opposite things. The reproduction's SQL is not recorded on the ticket, only its results.
questions.answer: DOWNGRADED after measurement -- and this corrects the driver's own earlier framing. The 13.3% raw-vs-FINAL overcount is a WHOLE-TABLE figure. On the slice this query actually touches, `hotlist WHERE status = 3`, the duplicate rate is only **0.33%**: raw 16,191,610 rows over 16,138,718 unique ids (52,892 duplicate rows), against FINAL+not-deleted 16,138,205 with zero duplicates. Soft-deletes at status = 3 are ~0. That makes sense -- Repossessed is a TERMINAL status, so those rows stop being updated and get merged, while the churny in-progress statuses carry the duplicates. Consequence: a missing FINAL cannot plausibly explain the reproduction's +14 (0.15%). Even a naive inflation ceiling would be 0.33% (~30 rows), and most duplicates collapse anyway because the recoveries CTE aggregates with max(hsl.created_at) and groups per (vin, agent) pair. The ticket's live-hotlist-drift explanation stands as the better one, and the route's validation evidence is NOT undermined. What survives as a real requirement: the port should still apply FINAL + _peerdb_is_deleted = 0 on the hotlist leg deliberately (it is correct, and cheap on this slice -- 1,049ms vs 559ms), and should NOT apply FINAL to hotlist_status_log or billing_events, where raw and FINAL counts are byte-identical and FINAL costs 10x for nothing. It remains unrecorded whether the comment-39117 reproduction used FINAL; that is now a hygiene note, not a blocker. CLOSED FOR GOOD by the full port measurement: with FINAL applied the total still reads 9,135 against the 9,116-9,117 Postgres target, and the drift rate reconciles across three readings at ~1.3-1.6/day in one direction. The +18 is live-hotlist drift, not a dedup artefact.
questions.how_to_close: Re-run the funnel twice against production read-only -- once with and once without FINAL + _peerdb_is_deleted = 0 on the hotlist leg -- and see which lands on 9,116-9,117. This also settles whether the route's validation evidence stands.

questions.q: What is the ClickHouse type of zod.public_billing_events.additional (the JSONB column holding claimed_by_org_id and vin in Postgres)? The table is absent from this repo's schema dump, so there is no local fixture to check. If it mirrors as String it needs JSONExtractString(); PG's `::int` cast ERRORS on a non-numeric value while a CH toInt32OrNull() would silently NULL that row -- a real, if low-probability, divergence in the port.
questions.answer: `additional` mirrors as a plain **String**, not a native JSON type (system.columns, driver-measured read-only 2026-09-08). Full mirror shape: id Int64, api_key_id Int32, success Bool, event_type String, additional String, ts Int64, plus the three _peerdb_* columns. So the port needs JSONExtractString(additional, 'vin') and, for claimed_by_org_id, JSONExtract-then-cast. Note the PG-vs-CH cast divergence stands: PG's `::int` ERRORS on a non-numeric value while toInt32OrNull() silently NULLs that row -- prefer a form that surfaces bad data rather than dropping it. Two incidental confirmations: `ts` really is an integer epoch (port rule 2 holds) and billing_events carries NO org_id, so the forwarder must come from api_keys.org_id exactly as the ticket says.
questions.how_to_close: DESCRIBE TABLE zod.public_billing_events read-only against production -- one statement, cheap.

questions.q: Do ClickHouse joins treat a NULL agent_org_id join key the way Postgres does (never matches, correctly excluding those claims from DB repos), or could join_use_nulls / the hash-join implementation match NULL-to-NULL and inflate the count?
questions.answer: No divergence -- ClickHouse behaves like Postgres. A synthetic INNER JOIN on a NULL key matched 0 rows under default settings AND with join_use_nulls = 1, while a NULL-vs-real-value control matched exactly 1 (driver-measured read-only 2026-09-08). Claims with an unresolved agent_org_id therefore cannot inflate DB repos. Candidate 1's concern is closed.
questions.how_to_close: An isolated empirical test against a seeded NULL-agent claim. Not inferable from static SQL.

REJECT the clarity.hotlist repo_date shortcut even though it is 5.9x cheaper (105.7M vs 664.3M read_rows, 5.54 vs 15.04 GB, 1.89 vs 2.50 GB memory): across 5 windows x 5 orgs it matched 23/25 but diverged -2 in April, and the diagnosis is decisive -- clarity.hotlist is missing 2 (vin, org) pairs outright, AND its repo_date differs from the status-transition date for 1,588 of 6,770 counted pairs (23%). It agrees only because '>= claim_date - 7' is loose enough to absorb the slack, so it is agreement by luck, not equivalence. Its repo_date comes from hotlist_meta (client-reported); backyard's definition is our own status transition. For a billing-adjacent figure reconciled against Brek's report, fidelity outranks the 3x scan. Record B as measured-and-rejected in the Build Record with the 23% figure so it is not re-proposed as a free win. See q8-recoveries-leg.md.

questions.q: The UTC calendar-month window rests on an unverified server default. Neither the clarity_clickhouse nor the public_clickhouse connection block in config/database.php sets a timezone, and the Postgres side never sets the session timezone GUC either (app.timezone=UTC does not control it). Should the port pass 'UTC' explicitly to every date function?
questions.answer: Yes -- pass 'UTC' explicitly to every date function. Driver-confirmed that neither the clarity_clickhouse nor the public_clickhouse block in config/database.php carries a timezone key, and the Postgres side never sets the session timezone GUC (app.timezone=UTC does not control it). Port rule 2 makes the UTC calendar month a hard requirement, so inheriting an implicit server default on either side is the one thing most likely to break it silently. Explicit UTC is cheap and strictly safer; taken as a driver decision rather than a question.
questions.driver_pick: Yes -- pass 'UTC' explicitly. Port rule 2 makes the UTC calendar month a hard requirement, and inheriting an implicit default on either side is the single biggest generic threat to it. This is cheap and strictly safer.

questions.q: NEW, surfaced by the merge. The ticket mandates one Cache::flexible([3600, 86400]) query per resolved window, but okf/concepts/company-metrics-dashboard.md warns that a card caching through its own path bypasses DashboardWidget::getCacheTTL() entirely -- including the collapse to a 10-second TTL while impersonating (the ladder is 1 year for sparkline buckets, 10 min for the headline, 10 s impersonating). Use Cache::flexible as the ticket says and accept that an impersonating admin sees a staler value here than on neighbouring cards, or use the base ladder and drop Cache::flexible?
questions.answer: ANSWERED from shipped precedent (DEV-2463's UniqueLprCaseClaims) -- and my framing of the hazard was BACKWARDS. I said the risk was an impersonating admin seeing a STALER value; the real risk is that getCacheTTL() collapses to 10s under admin_impersonator, which is SHORTER than the query's contended p99, so every impersonated re-render starts a fresh full scan (a stampede, not staleness). Keep Cache::flexible([3600, 86400]) as the ticket mandates, plus the four parts DEV-2463 shipped: (1) a getCacheTTL() override flooring the TTL (they use 60s); (2) a cold-path herd guard, because Cache::flexible locks ONLY its stale-refresh branch and a total miss is unlocked -- one full scan per entitled org per concurrent tab after a deploy or cache:clear; the guard must test BOTH $key and illuminate:cache:flexible:created:{$key}, which land in different Redis-cluster slots and can be evicted independently; (3) COLD_LOCK_SECONDS > CLICKHOUSE_TIMEOUT_QUERY and an explicit REFRESH_LOCK_SECONDS, since flexible()'s own refresh lock defaults to never expiring; (4) the window's identity in the cache key, or a month rollover serves a map whose newest bucket is absent and ?? 0 fabricates a zero. DO NOT inherit DEV-2463's constants: theirs are tuned to a ~40M-row query with a 9.3s contended p99, and DEV-2464's A1 measures 664M rows / 2.50 GB -- ~16x. Under-sizing COLD_BLOCK_SECONDS is the documented failure mode where every waiter times out and computes anyway. Measure this card's own p99 and re-derive. See q13-caching.md.

pg_tables: zod.public.billing_events (backyard-owned; upstream of the mirror only -- Clarity does not query Postgres on this route)
data_impact.mv_or_cdc_implications: All five are PeerDB CDC mirrors: ReplacingMergeTree(_peerdb_version, _peerdb_is_deleted), PRIMARY KEY id, ORDER BY id. Dedup is asynchronous, so raw reads can return duplicates. Driver-measured per table: hotlist raw 154,553,066 vs FINAL+not-deleted 136,362,585 (needs the discipline); hotlist_status_log and billing_events raw == FINAL+not-deleted exactly (do not today, and FINAL on the status log costs 10x for nothing). None of these four newly-needed tables has an Eloquent model with FiltersCdcDeletes except zod.public_hotlist (ZodPublicHotlist).
data_impact.indexes_relied_on: NONE usable. Every one of the five is ORDER BY id only -- org_id, vin, hotlist_id, api_key_id and created_at are all absent from the sort key, so no primary-index pruning is available for any predicate this query needs. This is the mechanical reason for the ~32s cold figure and why the caching rule is load-bearing.

resource_envelope.trigger: A new app/Clickhouse/Queries/* class joining production-scale CDC mirrors, driven from a Filament dashboard widget rendered on every Company Metrics page load. The ticket itself names this the epic's most expensive card.
resource_envelope.growth: hotlist and hotlist_status_log are live, continuously growing. Port rule 4 already records that DB repos reads live hotlist and drifts upward. No case-claim-specific growth curve was obtainable; carrying the repo's standing caution (PG-027 precedent: the fleet moved 29->43 kits and 11->12 orgs in a single day) against sizing to today's maximum.
resource_envelope.allocation_sketch: Not a scheduled command or job, so there is no accumulation risk -- PHP-side allocation is O(1), one integer, no per-row loop. The risk is per-execution QUERY cost. Per distinct (resolved window, org) cache key, Cache::flexible([3600, 86400]) allows at most one fresh computation per hour with stale-serve for 24h. The claims leg is bounded by the ts range (~15K claim rows/month platform-wide per the ticket's own cross-check). The recoveries leg must stay bounded to the small set of agent orgs present in that org's deduped claims -- backyard's recoveriesCte() docblock states this discipline explicitly ('never scan all status=3 hotlists for the agent orgs -- that is tens of millions of rows') and the port MUST preserve it. Since no sort key prunes, a careless port degrades to a near-full scan of 389M + 136M rows. Measured cost inputs: ~32s cold / 8.65s warm client wall clock for the whole funnel; a bare FINAL count on hotlist alone is 12.5s.
unresolved: Server-side read_rows / read_bytes / peak memory: UNKNOWN. readonly_user lacks READ ON REMOTE, so clusterAllReplicas(system.query_log) is denied. Only client wall clock has ever been measured. See q12.
Concurrency envelope: how many distinct orgs can independently cache-miss a ~32s query within the same fresh window has never been modelled or measured.
The added cost of FINAL on the hotlist leg, if q3 concludes it is required. A bare count already costs 12.5s; inside the join it is unmeasured.
The cost of any wide GROUP BY month sparkline query (q2 option c) is entirely unmeasured on the same 389M-row join.

design_consequences.finding: The org filter does not reduce the scan AT ALL -- A1 reads 664,270,998 rows whether scoped to one org or platform-wide, because every table involved is ORDER BY id and nothing prunes (matches okf/concepts/billing-events.md for billing_events). Per-org computation is therefore the worst possible shape: N orgs cache-missing = N x 15 GB and N x 2.5 GB memory for a query whose cost is identical to computing every org at once.
design_consequences.implication: Phase 3 should consider a BATCH shape -- one pass emitting all orgs (arrayJoin over [forwarder_org_id, agent_org_id] to attribute each claim to both sides, grouped by org and month), cached as a map, as ClientRankedMetricsBatch and BatchMonthlySparklineData already do. Turns N x 15 GB into 1 x 15 GB. Does not change the metric, only how often the scan is paid for. Interacts with q13: a shared batch map is a different caching object than a per-org Cache::flexible key.

design_consequences.finding: heldFlexible(), flexibleCreatedKey() and MIN_TTL_SECONDS are PRIVATE to UniqueLprCaseClaims; flexibleRefreshLock() is protected. DEV-2464 needs all of it and DEV-2463's docblock names DEV-2465 as a third user.
design_consequences.implication: Extract to a shared concern (e.g. Concerns/HeldFlexibleCache.php) rather than write a second copy -- the Redis-cluster two-key subtlety is exactly what rots in a duplicate. Constants stay per-card, calibrated per query. Code-organisation call; operator can veto.
